rule: This register is the stratum's own non-claims, recorded per surface as `measured` (a passing court covers the surface), `not-measured` (a surface this stratum names but no court reaches, so it is named `pending` rather than counted as passing) or `not-claimed` (explicitly outside this stratum -- including benchmark parity and assembly-versus-Rust equivalence). It is authored, not derived: the `PERFORMANCE-BOUNDARY-REGISTER` court in forensics/tools/phase19_courts.py re-reads the live courts registry and the four probe courts' evidence and fails the stratum if any recorded classification, surface key or stated count/evidence value here has drifted from what the courts actually show (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md sections 3.1, 3.5 and 3.6). A surface the courts do not reach is `not-measured` or `not-claimed`, never `measured`, and the register may not claim more than the courts above measured.

surfaces.surface: the three candidate CPU-capability names OPENSSL_ia32cap_P, OPENSSL_cpuid_setup and OPENSSL_ia32_cpuid
surfaces.finding: the candidate reaches none of the three (probe.reachable.*=0, CPUINFO: N/A), while the authority reaches all three through the -Wl,-u forced static link; the disposition is recorded, not substituted
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: the court records which names each side reaches under the fixed link, not that the candidate implements a CPU-capability surface. It is the `symbols_not_reached` census docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md section 4.2 records (sections 3.4 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the candidate's capability-derived selection under the OPENSSL_ia32cap facade (dispatch invariance under masking)
surfaces.finding: the authority's capability-derived selection moves with the facade (sel.aes128cbcsha1.null 0 -> 1 with AES-NI masked); the candidate's does not, because the reduced engine does not model OPENSSL_ia32cap masking
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: this is a bounded audit of the capability surface at the three sets the court drives, not a parity claim and not an assembly-versus-Rust equivalence claim (sections 3.4 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the selection each path makes under the reference capability set
surfaces.finding: 0 divergences at the reference set: the authority and the candidate select identically across the legacy constructor, provider fetch, name lookup and cipher/digest context paths
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: a bounded comparison of selection over the sets the court drives, not a parity claim and not an assembly-versus-Rust equivalence claim (sections 3.4 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the selection each path makes under the AES-NI-cleared and fully-cleared capability sets
surfaces.finding: masking the AES-NI bit moves the authority's AES-*-CBC-HMAC-* fetch/legacy/lookup selection to NULL and does not move the candidate's; the 88 differences per faulted set are recorded, not failed
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: the candidate reads CPUID directly and does not model the mask, so its selection does not move; that disposition is a recorded divergence rather than a parity claim (sections 3.4 and 3.6).

surfaces.finding: no engine is configured and the reduced engine does not export the enumeration the probe would need, so the engine path is not driven
surfaces.note: not-measured: the engine path is named but no court reaches it, so it is recorded rather than assumed; a name that cannot be driven is `pending`, never counted as passing (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md sections 3.1 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the symmetric and digest paths (AES-128/256-CBC, AES-128/256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-256)
surfaces.finding: each of these paths' library-side work vector equals the authority's -- the counting allocator records the same malloc/realloc/byte counts
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: the counting allocator observes heap operations, not total CPU instructions, and the block counts are input-implied; agreement on this instrument is not a benchmark-parity claim (sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the two divergent-work paths (a P-256 scalar multiplication and an RSA-1024 private decrypt)
surfaces.finding: these paths' library-side work vectors differ from the authority's (ec-p256-mul allocs 3 vs 4, bytes 2121 vs 160; rsa-1024-private allocs 46 vs 31, bytes 4541 vs 2669) and are recorded as findings, so the property is NOT_CLAIMED
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: the court passes as an instrument while recording every path whose deterministic work differs from the authority's as a finding; a passing RT-PERFORMANCE-WORK must never be read as 'performance parity achieved' (sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the counting-allocator instrument's resolution against a deliberately slowed path
surfaces.finding: the deliberately slowed control-extra-pass variant is caught on the counting allocator (allocs and bytes differ) while the reference arm equals the authority's recorded aes-128-cbc vector
surfaces.note: measured, not claimed: the verdict is about the instrument's resolution and makes no throughput or benchmark-parity claim; a control that cannot tell a slow path from a fast one is `fail`, never a vacuous `pass` (sections 3.2 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: benchmark / throughput parity with the authority
surfaces.finding: no throughput ratio to the authority is asserted anywhere in this stratum
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a passing performance court is a bounded deterministic-work comparison at the resolution it declares, and this stratum makes no benchmark-parity claim (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md section 0).

surfaces.surface: assembly-versus-Rust equivalence of the per-CPU paths
surfaces.finding: the authority's per-CPU assembly paths and the candidate's reduced implementations are not asserted to be the same work
surfaces.note: not-claimed: the two implementations are not asserted to perform identical work; this stratum makes no assembly-versus-Rust equivalence claim (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md section 0).

surfaces.finding: no verdict is ever taken from elapsed time alone
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a wall-clock measurement on a shared host is not reproducible, so the courts count deterministic work instead; where a wall-clock figure is recorded at all no verdict is taken from it alone (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md section 3.3).

surfaces.finding: the counting allocator observes heap operations, not total CPU instructions
surfaces.note: not-claimed: the instrument is a counting CRYPTO allocator plus input-implied block counts, a deterministic instruction-path proxy rather than a total instruction count (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md sections 1 and 3.3).

surfaces.finding: this stratum claims no parity for any symbol
surfaces.note: not-claimed: PARITY_VERIFIED is not claimed for any symbol by this stratum, which owns no exported symbol and measures the implementation the strata before it completed (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md sections 0 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: a guarantee about throughput or about the recorded boundary
surfaces.finding: a register entry is a record of a boundary, not a guarantee
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a register entry records a boundary and a passing performance court is a measurement result; neither guarantees throughput or that the boundary cannot be crossed (docs/PHASE-19-SUBPHASES.md section 0).
